newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Contal defying odds. [CORRECTED 16:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Contal defying odds. [CORRECTED 16:34 GMT]

text.p: High operating margins are the secret to bottler Grupo Continental's almost 82 percent nominal rise in stock value in 1996, company finance director Miquel Angel Rabago Vite told Reuters.

Contal, a Coca-Cola bottler based in Tampico, defied the odds last year, outpacing a Mexican stock market that crept ahead just 21 percent last year in nominal terms, but lost ground in real terms thanks to 28 percent inflation.
"To explain this, one must consider that Contal's margins are the highest among Mexican bottlers," Rabago said.
Contal came in second place in stock returns among Mexican bottlers after Coca-Cola (correct from "PepsiCo") bottler Argos.

During the depths of Mexico's financial crisis in 1995, when inflation was galloping, Contal lifted its operating margins to 14.6 percent from 9.8 percent in 1994. By the third quarter in 1996, the company's margins hit 18 percent.
"Our market participation is among the highest, which reaffirms Contal's leadership. And although (the margins) are high, they keep growing," Rabago said.

Contal has the largest territorial Coca-Cola bottling franchise in Mexico, and controls a market of 11 million in the central states of Durango, Coahuila, Zacatecas, San Luis Potosi, Aguascalientes and Jalisco.
In November 1995, Forbes magazine included Contal on its list of the 100 best small companies in the world.

"Contal's market participation is one of the highest in Latin America, we think with the introduction of new presentations it can raise its participation in flavors and consolidate its dominance of colas," Bear Stearns analysts Carlos Laboy and Hector Tassinari said in a telephone interview.
Contal says it holds an estimated 87 to 94 percent stake in cola sales and a 49 to 72 percent stake in other flavors in the northern and southern zones where it has a presence.

"In the central zone, the company has a good opportunity to raise its participation in flavors, the same as in the western zone where it has a 33 percent stake in the area (of flavors)," the analysts said.
Rabago said Coca-Cola's decision to boost its stake in Contal to 17.3 percent from 11.7 percent shows confidence in the small company and its profitability and capacity to grow.

Analysts have also noted that in the last months of 1996, Coca Cola chose Contal to launch in the Mexican market two important products, the flavored drink Chispa and the Ciel brand of purified water.

"Contal margins could continue growing, because among other reasons water is more profitable than flavored drinks," Laboy and Tassinari said, estimating a 19 to 20 percent growth in the stock's value in 1997.
Another important factor for 1997 could be the continuing reduction of costs in colas as packing costs drop, especially in non-returnable bottles, they said.
The analysts said Contal's sugar engineers are the most efficient in the industry.
